title: CustomDomainConnect
wrapsNative: VStack (or a Form) of MonarchTextField, MonarchDomainProgress, MonarchDnsRecordTable and MonarchButton, with confirmationDialog(_:isPresented:titleVisibility:actions:message:) for removal
summary: A recipe, not a component: connect a custom domain by entering it, copying the DNS records, verifying, and following its progress to live, with removal behind a confirmation.
whenToUse: On the domain settings screen of a product that serves pages, booking sites or help centres on the customer's own domain.
whenNotToUse: For showing only the state of a domain that is already set up, use MonarchDomainProgress alone; for DNS records with no connection flow, use MonarchDnsRecordTable.
api: MonarchTextField.init(_ label: String, text: Binding<String>, prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, isSecure: Bool = false)

MonarchDomainProgress.init(_ host: String, stage: MonarchDomainStage, problems: [MonarchDomainProblem] = [], dnsFound: MonarchDomainDnsSnapshot? = nil, checkedAt: Date? = nil, now: Date? = nil, isRechecking: Bool = true, notify: MonarchDomainNotify? = nil, labels: MonarchDomainProgressLabels = MonarchDomainProgressLabels())

states.name: enter
states.description: A Domain field with an example prompt and help; Connect domain is disabled until the text looks like a host, and a URL or a path shows the error under the field.

states.name: records
states.description: After connecting: MonarchDomainProgress at the DNS step, the records as cards with copy buttons, Verify DNS and Remove domain.

states.name: verifying
states.description: The app checks DNS and moves the stage (dns, ownership, certificate, page, live); records show Found or Waiting from isFound.

states.name: live
states.description: MonarchDomainProgress shows every step done; Verify DNS is disabled.

states.name: remove
states.description: A confirmation dialog with the domain in its title and a destructive Remove domain.

appearance: Every part keeps its Monarch styling: the field and buttons as elsewhere, the progress steps with tone icons and words, the records as cards on the surface colour. The confirmation dialog is the system's.
platformNotes: The web ships CustomDomainConnect as one pattern with domain normalisation (punycode, scheme and path stripping), a four-step stepper, a provider picker with product-written instructions, async onConnect, onVerify and onRemove, and its own messages. On iOS it is a recipe so the product keeps its own networking and copy: the app normalises the host (URLComponents can strip a pasted scheme and path), calls its API, and sets the stage and each record's isFound from its checks. MonarchDomainProgress replaces the web stepper and status badge. A provider picker is a Picker with .menu style above the records. Removal uses confirmationDialog, the iOS pattern for a destructive choice. Marked experimental because it is a product flow, not a primitive, until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: The Domain field reads its label, value, help and error; the error has an icon and text.
The DNS records heading has the header trait; each record value and name is read with its copy button, as MonarchDnsRecordTable does.
MonarchDomainProgress reads each step with its state and announces when a step completes.
The disabled Connect domain and Verify DNS buttons are read as dimmed.
The removal dialog is the system dialog, with the destructive action announced as such.
edgeCases: People paste full URLs: strip the scheme, path and port before validating, or show the error as the recipe does.
DNS changes can take hours: keep the records visible while the stage is dns, and recheck on a timer with MonarchDomainProgress.recheckInterval(for:).
Several domains on one screen: give each its own section and include the host in the removal title.

parityExceptions.reason: The web draws the four steps as a row with each name beside its circle, which needs about 420 points; a phone column has 306, so each name sits under its circle (the stepper's stacked row) and the compact form takes over at larger text sizes.
parityExceptions.convention: HIG: a phone layout stacks a label under its control rather than shrinking it
